newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia mulls limiting foreign fund flow to T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Russia mulls limiting foreign fund flow to T-bills.

text.p: The Russian Central Bank is developing measures which would allow it to limit foreign capital coming into the government securities market without breaking pledges to the IMF, central bankers said on Monday.

Central Bank chairman Sergei Dubinin told reporters the measures, developed by the bank's credit committee, would be prepared in a month or two and would have to be approved by its board of directors.

The Central Bank board has adopted a timetable for liberalising the domestic T-bill and bond market to foreign investors, who will be able to repatriate funds without conditions by the beginning of next year.

"But we have the complete right in accordance with this article (Article Eight of the International Monetary Fund) to control and even take measures, if necessary, to regulate movement of capital through entrance and exit (from the country)," Dubinin said.
"It might be expedient to name limits," he said.

Article Eight of the IMF charter effectively requires Russia to liberalise repatriation of invested funds, but bankers said they could stop money coming into the country and were considering the measure for fear of sudden foreign capital flight.
"In some sense because of the Mexican syndrome (sudden capital flight by foreigners), we are worried about more dependence on foreign investors," Dubinin said.
"Now the market has achieved a certain stability, conservative investors are in the market, investing from $700 million to $1 billion per month. That is a stable situation which suits us," he said.
Deputy Chairman Andrei Kozlov told a separate news conference that foreigners represented slightly more than 15 percent of the market and were slowly increasing their presence.
He said the bank could put outright limits on conversion of foreign currency into roubles but under no circumstances would limit repatriation of invested funds and profits.
